subject: Creativity
title: Wicked Problems: When Design Thinking Meets Chaos
description: Learn Wicked Problems: When Design Thinking Meets Chaos in one minute.

hook.text: How do you solve poverty? Climate change? Healthcare inequality?

buildup.text: Horst Rittel coined 'wicked problems' in 1973 — problems with no clear definition, no stopping rule, and no right answer.

discovery.text: Each attempt to solve a wicked problem changes the problem itself.

twist.text: Traditional engineering approaches fail on wicked problems. They need design thinking's iterative, empathetic approach.

climax.text: You can't 'solve' wicked problems. You can only improve them — continuously, iteratively, and humbly.

punchline.text: Some problems can't be solved. They can only be managed — wisely and endlessly.

quiz.question: What defines a 'wicked problem'?
options: It has no clear definition, no stopping rule, and changes when addressed
